title: brassica rupestris subsp. villosa
intro: Brassica rupestris subsp. villosa, commonly known as Alpine Cabbage, is a subspecies of wild cabbage native to the mountainous regions of Europe. It has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include reducing inflammation and improving digestion due to its rich content of antioxidants and fiber. The therapeutic actions of Alpine Cabbage are attributed to its ability to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, making it a potential treatment for various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Brassica rupestris subsp. villosa include glucosinolates, isothiocyanates, and flavonoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
